title: A worker brief names a known whole-suite failure that is not a test, such as the seconds ceiling, so the worker files no duplicate bug
goal: backlog.py brief and dispatch take --known-suite TEXT=BUG beside --known TEST=BUG (TEXT a suite-level failure that is no test, such as the darwin seconds ceiling, BUG the bug filed for it) and print it in the brief's known failures section whose closing line tells the worker that a listed failure gets no new bug

run: import subprocess,sys;p=subprocess.run(['python3','_tools/backlog.py','brief','ST-cr6lmafy','--known-suite','suite seconds budget exceeded=BG-w6z2zc6r'],capture_output=True,text=True);s=p.stdout.split('## Known failing',1)[-1].split('## Fixed rules',1)[0];sys.exit(0 if p.returncode==0 and 'suite seconds budget exceeded' in s and 'BG-w6z2zc6r' in s else 1)

gates.question: Does --known-suite accept a BUG that is no backlog item, as --known does?
options: accept: the text is printed with the id as given, like --known
refuse: a BUG that is no backlog item exits 2 naming it
gates.recommendation: accept: the text is printed with the id as given, like --known
gates.answer: accept: the text is printed with the id as given, like --known

gates.question: How does the brief print a --known-suite failure and its closing line?
options: line '- suite-level, no test: TEXT: BUG label'; closing line 'A failure listed here gets no new bug; a failure not named here is yours to file as a bug.'
reuse the TEST line form with TEXT in backticks, closing line unchanged
gates.recommendation: line '- suite-level, no test: TEXT: BUG label'; closing line 'A failure listed here gets no new bug; a failure not named here is yours to file as a bug.'

notes: Retrospective of SP-7n3d4jte (2026-10-12): the ST-b27c527d worker filed BG-6jaaptm6 for the darwin seconds ceiling although its brief's --probe named BG-ucwq6kga and BG-w6z2zc6r; --known takes only TEST=BUG, so the ceiling had to go in a free-text probe.
